title: Playing head arrangements: sleeving and the blue book
summary: Phillips explains that Jordan's band, like Mr. Young's, played head arrangements learned by ear, which they called sleeving or the blue book.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Everything they played mostly was a head. They got together head stuff.
Did they do a lot of rehearsing?
Yeah. But see, it don't take... If you've
got a kind of head thing, it don't take a whole lot of rehearsing. If you're sleevin', you ain't got to read that music...
That means playing by ear? Learning heads?
Yeah. And Mr. Young called it in the blue book. He said, 'Let's get in the blue book.'
What did he mean by that?
We got a whole lot of tunes with sleeves... You have a whole lot of sleeves in the band; you don't have no music.

Yeah, head arrangements. Like 'Tiger Rag,' the Blues, some kind of movement on the Blues -- there was all kind of Blues. Then we'd have like 'How Come You Do Me Like You Do' -- those kind of easy sleevin' tunes.
You'd know them by the head.
